lead.headline: Sensex falls more than 1,000 points as oil climbs after the Hormuz rejection
lead.deck: The first session since reports that Trump turned down Iran's seven-day plan. PSU banks and autos led the fall; the 10-year bond yield hit a two-year high.
lead.short: The Sensex dropped more than 1,000 points in the first hour on Monday and the Nifty fell below 22,850, wiping close to ₹6 lakh crore off listed companies. Brent crude rose again after reports over the weekend that Trump had rejected Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and expects to resume bombing after the US midterms. PSU banks and carmakers fell hardest.
more: Foreign investors sold ₹3,693 crore of Indian shares on Friday, and the Nifty had just logged its seventh weekly loss in a row, its longest losing run since early 2020. India's 10-year government bond yield rose to its highest in more than two years, and the rupee held just short of 96 to the dollar with the RBI selling dollars.
The fall came despite strong growth figures earlier this month, 7.8% in the April to June quarter. The next scheduled test for rates is the RBI's policy decision on 7 October.

why.text: Oil is the fastest route from the Iran war to Indian prices, the rupee and your portfolio; today is the first clean read of the rejection.

seconds.headline: Kohli 139 not out and Gill 110 take India past 295 with 50 balls left
seconds.short: India beat West Indies by eight wickets in Thiruvananthapuram, chasing 296 at 300 for 2. Kohli, who promised before the series to bat more freely, made 139 not out and Shubman Gill 110, his 10th ODI hundred in 67 innings. Kuldeep Yadav took 4 for 40 on his ODI return after Justin Greaves (101) and John Campbell put on 135 for the first wicket.
more: Naman Dhir made his ODI debut and Nitish Kumar Reddy led the pace attack. The second match is in Guwahati on Wednesday at 14:00 IST.

why.text: Kohli's first ODI of the new cycle answered the question about his role in one innings.

seconds.headline: The three-day bank strike is off; branches open as normal
seconds.short: Bank unions deferred the 28 to 30 September strike after a late Sunday meeting with the Indian Banks' Association. The two sides agreed to set up a high-level committee on declaring all Saturdays holidays, the main demand for a five-day week, and to take up officers' incentive pay and other pending issues.

why.text: Branch work you put off for the strike can be done this week, before the half-year close on Wednesday.

seconds.headline: Supreme Court declines to pause the UPI merchant fee, asks the Centre to explain it
seconds.short: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant refused an interim stay on the 0.4% fee on merchant payments above ₹2,000, due from 15 October, and gave the Centre and the RBI four weeks to file replies. The court called it "less a legal and more a technical issue" after the government said 96% of users would stay exempt.

why.text: The fee starts on 15 October as planned; any change now comes after the Centre's reply.

seconds.headline: Europe win the Laver Cup 13–5 without Alcaraz needing to play on Sunday
seconds.short: Flavio Cobolli and Jakub Mensik won the opening doubles and Alexander Zverev beat Learner Tien 7–6, 6–3 to take Europe to 13. It is Yannick Noah's first title as Europe captain and Europe's sixth in nine editions, a year after losing in San Francisco.

why.text: Alcaraz's saved match points on Saturday proved the decisive swing; his next event is the China Open.

briefs.headline: USA win 9.5 of 12 singles to take the Presidents Cup 17–13
briefs.text: It was the largest final-day comeback in the event's history and the Americans' 11th straight win; Collin Morikawa and 21-year-old Jackson Koivun turned key matches on the back nine.

monday.mood: Indian shares sold off from the open: the Sensex lost more than 1,000 points in the first hour and the Nifty broke below 22,850, with PSU banks and autos worst. The cues were all one way: Brent back up on the Hormuz rejection, US and Indian bond yields at multi-year highs, and foreign investors selling ₹3,693 crore on Friday.
weekend: Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz, reports said on Friday night, and told aides he expects bombing to resume after the midterms; oil rose again on Monday.
China cut tariffs on US corn, wheat, meat and dairy on Monday but left soybeans out, the first step after the Trump-Xi summit.

movers.answer: Fell 9.5% on 25 Sep ahead of a rights-issue board meeting and slipped again on 28 Sep with the market while the board met.
Fell with the broad market on oil and yields; no sector-specific trigger reported. Vodafone Idea was down about 2.8% despite launching free international roaming.
